text:
alisa: heads up — putting a sketch of a cost-aware slotting + routing proposal for telemetry replays. want quick reactions before i turn this into a PR.

alisa: tl;dr: prioritize cheap slot candidates (cpu-preemptible / low-gpu-util nodes) for low-urgency backfills, route urgent tenant slices to reserved capacity. aim: reduce egress compute cost by ~20% without blowing our latency SLO for high-priority replays.

mike: curious — how do you define low-urgency? is it age-based or SLA-based?

alisa: good q. plan is multi-signal: age (days late), customer tier (prod vs dev), and whether downstream dashboards are behind SLO. fallback to owner tag if signals missing.

david: what about shard affinity? routing off cheap nodes will increase cross-shard shuffle and might hurt throughput.

alisa: agreed — we keep strong preference for local-shard-first. only consider cross-shard when local slot waiting > X minutes OR when tenant is explicitly low-priority.

jana: are we changing quota semantics? sounds like we need a new quota bucket for ‘preemptible-replay’ so we can throttle separately.

mike: yes please separate buckets. otherwise we get noisy-neighbor where cheap slots steal capacity and block reserved jobs.

alisa: exactly. proposal: add two new quota labels: replay:slot_type={reserved, preemptible} and replay:urgency={low,normal,high}. Console exposes both as dropdowns in replay job config.

sophia: UI note — for rollouts UX, default should be nearest-equivalent to current behavior. i.e., if user doesn't pick, map legacy priority -> normal/reserved mapping. avoid surprising devs.

mike: also need visibility in Console: per-job expected cost estimate and estimated time-to-completion for both reserved and preemptible routes. ops will ask for that in 5m. :grin:

alisa: agreed. early estimator can be heuristic: cost_per_token * est_tokens + node_premium. we'll refine from telemetry. add a backend field `estimated_cost_cents` returned by the internal API.

david: how do we handle preemption? if a preemptible node dies mid-replay, do we retry automatically on reserved? that could double-charge.

alisa: plan: allow a retry policy with three options: fail-fast, retry-on-preemptible, escalate-to-reserved. default = retry-on-preemptible with exponential backoff up to N attempts, then escalate. will surface in audit logs.

replay-bot: started replay 1777778001 for tenant: acme-corp slice: 2024-03-12 -> slot: preemptible-a

jana: logging/telemetry — we need a per-slice cost tag and a reason code when escalated so billing matches. add `replay.cost_tag` and `replay.escalation_reason` to events.

alisa: yep adding those. also propose a new dashboard tab: Replay Queue -> Slots by type, Preemptions/hr, Escalations, Avg cost per slice.

sophia: question on rollout: feature flag gated? prefer feature-flag + tenant opt-in for first 2 weeks.

mike: agree. rollout plan: alpha for infra team, then 10% of low-priority tenants, then 100% after 2w and metrics look good. will need an emergency-off flag.

david: do we need any API changes? sounds like new params on /v1/replays: slot_type_hint, urgency, retry_policy. keep them optional.

alisa: exactly. sample request: 
```
POST /v1/replays
{
  "tenant": "acme-corp",
  "slice": "2024-03-12",
  "slot_type_hint": "preemptible",
  "urgency": "low",
  "retry_policy": "escalate_on_fail"
}
```

jana: thumbs up for JSON shape. add `estimated_cost_cents` to response.

mike: we should simulate at least 24h of preemption traces against replay scheduler before enabling.

alisa: i'll wire up a small simulator that replays our last month of replays and injects preemption rates per-region. aim to have sim results by EOD Fri.

sophia: +1. also add a Console banner explaining that low-urgency replays may take longer under cost mode.

david: one last thing — quota enforcement: if preemptible bucket exhausted, should we queue or escalate? queue seems fine but add visibility.

alisa: queue by default; escalate if queue_time > threshold (configurable by tenant). good catch.

mike: ok i'm happy with this direction. can you open a draft PR with the schema changes and scheduler patch? i'll review.

alisa: will do. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
